clue.text: Dog's bottom seen in twisting to catch jay, we hear

definitions.note: read as 'Dog is', the 's standing for is

parts.note: the base of something is its bottom

indicators.note: to catch says the turned pair closes round the next piece
twisting turns the little word in round so it reads backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: we hear tells us only the sound of the bird's name is wanted

parts.note: the bird jay is said like the letter J

explanation.surface: A dog's backside is spotted squirming as it tries to snatch a jay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen' is only a link. 'twisting' turns IN round, and 'to catch' puts the letter J, which the bird's name sounds like, inside that turned pair.
explanation.definitionFit: The basenji is a small African hunting breed known as the barkless dog.

clue.text: Weapons attacking team in North London

definitions.meaning: a store of weapons and ammunition
the Premier League football club based in Islington, North London

explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a stockpile of arms, and it is also the name of a North London football club.

clue.text: Bacterium in silo certain to come up

indicators.note: to come up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words silo certain

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A germ is lurking in a grain silo, bound to surface eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft lacked an indicator for the hidden step; 'in' supplies it. In a down clue 'to come up' reads ILOCE from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: E. coli is a common gut bacterium, a frequent cause of food poisoning.

clue.text: Dramatist once 16 under the throne

indicators.note: in a down clue, under puts this piece below the previous one

parts.note: throne is slang for a lavatory, as is john
16 across is the word happy, and gay once meant happy

explanation.surface: A playwright of old sits beneath the royal seat, happy as anything.
explanation.walkthrough: John Gay (1685-1732) wrote The Beggar's Opera. 'the throne' is jocular slang for a toilet; JOHN is American slang for the same.
explanation.definitionFit: John Gay was an eighteenth-century English playwright and poet, so a dramatist of the past.

clue.text: Deception where I'm invisible in slim figure

indicators.note: invisible in says these letters vanish from inside the word slim

parts.note: taken as written
the letters of I'm, apostrophe aside
eight is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: A trick in which a person turns invisible inside a thin outline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where' is only a link; 'invisible in' removes the letters of I'm from inside slim, and 'figure' is a number spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight, as in sleight of hand, is skilful trickery or deceit.

clue.text: Scottish girl, fool in romance

indicators.note: in says the fool goes inside the romance word

parts.note: to romance is to tell fanciful tales, so to lie
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A girl from Scotland plays the fool in a love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'romance' is used as a verb meaning to exaggerate or fib.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassie is the Scots word for a young woman or girl.

clue.text: English couple Britain treated as drunk

definitions.note: an adjective here, as the answer can be

indicators.note: treated says the letters are processed into a new order

parts.note: two lots of E, the abbreviation for English
taken as written

explanation.surface: An English pair cure Britain of something, as if they had had a few.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges EE plus BRITAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Inebriate, as an adjective, is a formal word for intoxicated.

clue.text: Bound to accept peaky tor's peak — is a peak!

indicators.note: to accept says the leap takes the next letters inside it

parts.note: to bound is to hop
peaky is British slang for looking ill

indicators.note: the peak of a word is its top, its first letter

explanation.surface: A climber reaches a tor's summit feeling poorly, and exclaims about the height.
explanation.walkthrough: HOP accepts ILL plus T (the top of tor). 'peaky' means pale and unwell in British English; a tor is a rocky hill.
explanation.definitionFit: The top of a hill is a peak, the summit point.

clue.text: Mistake over order, chip wrong — a bloomer

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts this piece above the next one

parts.note: a slip is a small mistake

indicators.note: wrong says these letters are set out in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone makes a slip over a takeaway order, getting the chips wrong: a real blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges ORDER and CHIP into PERORCHID. 'bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The slipper orchid is a flowering plant, so a thing that blooms.

clue.text: What's tagged on hoodlums, like a bad smell

parts.note: as means like
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: Something hangs round young thugs like a nasty whiff.
explanation.walkthrough: An ASBO is a British Anti-Social Behaviour Order, often enforced with an electronic tag.
explanation.definitionFit: Courts imposed these orders on troublemakers, sometimes monitored with electronic tags, so they were pinned on thugs.

clue.text: How might one summon the devil, dammit?

definitions.text: How might one summon the devil
definitions.meaning: a whimsical reading: chimes rung from the underworld to call up Satan

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an exclamation of annoyance, and literally means chimes of the inferno.

clue.text: See 16
Shame about Olympic venue — right as the prime concern

indicators.note: about says the shame word goes round the others

parts.note: a shame is a pity
Rio de Janeiro hosted the 2016 Olympics

explanation.surface: It's a pity about the Olympic site; doing the right thing comes first.
explanation.walkthrough: PITY goes about RIO and R: P(RIOR)ITY. 'as the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A priority is the matter treated as most important, the main concern.

clue.text: Those let down by tatty odd bits in trousers

indicators.note: in places those letters inside the trousers

parts.note: flares are bell-bottomed trousers

indicators.note: odd bits takes the first, third and fifth letters of tatty

explanation.surface: Some people are disappointed by scruffy oddments stuffed in their trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let down' suggests disappointed, but here it means deflated. Flares are wide-bottomed trousers popular in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyres let down have been deflated, so flat ones are those let down.

clue.text: Peg gripping trousers, first of dungarees shown

indicators.note: gripping says the peg holds the trousers inside it

parts.note: a golf tee is a peg
Levis are a brand of jeans

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of dungarees

explanation.surface: A clothes peg clips jeans to the line, with dungarees hung out first.
explanation.walkthrough: TEE grips LEVIS to give TELEVISE, then D.
explanation.definitionFit: Something televised has been broadcast, that is screened on TV.

clue.text: Death of a dwarf, as last page of fairy tale?

indicators.note: of joins the two pieces, the dwarf's word coming first

parts.note: Happy is one of the seven dwarfs in Snow White
death is an end, an ending

explanation.surface: A dwarf dies, as on the closing page of a fairy story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link. Happy is one of the seven dwarfs.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairy tales traditionally close with everyone living contentedly ever after, so the closing page shows this.

clue.text: Time to identify all the characters

definitions.meaning: a period, as in a ... of sunshine
to name every letter of a word in turn

explanation.definitionFit: A spell is a stretch of time, and to spell a word is to give its letters.

clue.text: Soil cut up with old instrument

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, reads the word from the bottom

parts.note: to lop is to cut
the lute is an old stringed instrument

explanation.surface: Earth gets chopped up alongside an antique musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LOP into POL. 'with' is a link. 'Soil' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To soil something is to dirty or contaminate it.

clue.text: Some sites needing redevelopment, as it would appear

indicators.note: redevelopment rebuilds these letters in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A few building plots seem to need rebuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means apparently, as things appear.

clue.text: Hot drink raised in a bit of whisky this evening

indicators.note: in places them inside the small measure

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits

indicators.note: raised, in a down clue, turns the pieces upwards

parts.note: gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A hot toddy is brought up in a dram of whisky tonight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses HGIN into NIGH, and 'in' puts that inside TOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means on the evening of today.

clue.text: Muslim's inconceivable renouncement, with which a child's constructive

parts.note: Mecca is the holy city of Islam, Muslims' destination
the holy city followed by a refusal, which no Muslim would say

explanation.surface: A Muslim's unthinkable rejection, paired with a child's building toy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mecca? No!' is the renouncement a Muslim would never make.
explanation.definitionFit: Meccano is a construction toy of metal strips and nuts and bolts.

clue.text: Fungus in parcel turned up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: turned up, in a down clue, reads the package word from the bottom

parts.note: a pack is a parcel

explanation.surface: A mushroom is found in a package that's been opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses PACK into KCAP.
explanation.definitionFit: The ink cap is a mushroom whose gills dissolve into black liquid.

clue.text: Eastern European river in oil disaster, far side obscured

indicators.note: in places the river inside
the far side is the last letter, which is hidden away

parts.note: a slick is a spill of oil on water
the Avon is an English river

explanation.surface: An East European waterway suffers an oil spill whose far bank is out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: SLICK loses its end, K, leaving SLIC, which takes AVON.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavonic means relating to the Slavs of eastern Europe and their languages.

clue.text: See something that's melted, then?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a playful description of whatever is no longer frozen water

explanation.definitionFit: To notice is to see, and the answer split in two says the stuff isn't frozen.

clue.text: Job cut to protect former state

indicators.note: to protect says the shortened job surrounds the next piece
cut docks the last letter

parts.note: a task is a job
ex means former

explanation.surface: Job cuts are made to shield an old state employee.
explanation.walkthrough: TASK cut to TAS holds EX: T(EX)AS. 'former' looks to qualify state but gives EX.
explanation.definitionFit: Texas is one of the fifty states of the USA, an example of a state, and once an independent republic.

clue.text: Spooner sees a little jumping as sycophancy

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the starts of words, so the opening sounds trade places

parts.note: some means a little
bucking is jumping, as a horse does

explanation.surface: Spooner watches a bit of leaping, seeing it as fawning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some bucking' with its first sounds swapped is said 'bum sucking'. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumsucking is vulgar British slang for toadying, fawning servility.

clue.text: Kiss while holding mistletoe, only the first time it happens?

indicators.note: holding puts the next letter inside

parts.note: as means while

indicators.note: only the first takes the opening letter of mistletoe

explanation.surface: A kiss under the mistletoe, but only the first time it happens.
explanation.walkthrough: XAS holds M: X(M)AS. Kissing under mistletoe is a Christmas custom.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas is the season of mistletoe kisses, so the time this happens.

clue.text: Again take on study — choose to pursue it

indicators.note: to pursue it puts the choice word after the study word

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
to opt is to choose

explanation.surface: Someone takes up a course again, choosing to follow it.
explanation.walkthrough: To read a subject is British for studying it at university.
explanation.definitionFit: To readopt is to adopt once more, take on again.

clue.text: Helping of chipolatas topmost, not going anywhere

indicators.note: Helping of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A serving of the finest little sausages, and nobody's moving.
explanation.walkthrough: Chipolatas are small thin British sausages.
explanation.definitionFit: Something halted is stationary, not moving anywhere.
